facts.statement: The genus Patagotitan was described by Carballido and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Carballido et al., 2017

facts.statement: Patagotitan is a titanosaurian sauropod from the Early Cretaceous Albian stage of the Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Patagotitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: A partial lower femur was discovered in 2010 by farm laborer Aurelio Hernández near La Flecha, Argentina, approximately 250 km west of Trelew.
facts.quote: A part of a lower femur was discovered in 2010 by a farm laborer, Aurelio Hernández, in the desert near La Flecha, Argentina, about 250 km west of Trelew.

facts.statement: Excavations uncovered more than 200 fossils, comprising 130 sauropod bones and 57 theropod teeth.
facts.quote: More than 200 fossils, including 130 sauropod bones and 57 theropod teeth, were uncovered.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in rock layers dated to approximately 101.62 million years ago, corresponding to the latest Albian age of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The rock layers at the La Flecha site belong to the Cerro Castaño Member of the Cerro Barcino Formation, and were specifically dated to approximately 101.62 million years in age (corresponding to the latest Albian age of the Cretaceous).

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalogued as MPEF-PV 3400, is a partial skeleton from sediment layer FLV3 lacking the skull.
facts.quote: One skeleton from FLV3 was designated as the holotype specimen of a new species, and was catalogued as MPEF-PV 3400.

facts.statement: In 2017, a team led by José Luis Carballido named the remains as the type species Patagotitan mayorum.
facts.quote: In 2017, José Luis Carballido, Diego Pol, Alejandro Otero, Ignacio Alejandro Cerda, Leonardo Salgado, Alberto Carlos Garrido, Jahandar Ramezani, Néstor Ruben Cúneo and Javier Marcelo Krause named these remains as the type species of a new genus, Patagotitan mayorum.

facts.statement: The generic name Patagotitan combines a reference to Patagonia with the Greek word for Titan to reflect the animal's strength and large size.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to Patagonia with a Greek Titan for the "strength and large size" of this titanosaur.

facts.statement: The specific name mayorum honors the Mayo family, who owned the La Flecha ranch.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Mayo family, owners of La Flecha ranch.

facts.statement: Patagotitan is distinguished from close relatives by unique features in its back and tail vertebrae, shoulder blades, forelimb bones, and hindlimb bones.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished from its close relatives by a suite of unique characteristics in its back and tail vertebrae, scapulae and humeri in the forelimb, and ischia and femora in the hindlimb.

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived in a forested floodplain environment dominated by coniferous trees.
facts.quote: In life, Patagotitan lived in a forested region on a floodplain that was dominated by coniferous trees.

facts.statement: Preliminary estimates suggested Patagotitan reached a length of 37 meters and a weight of 69 tonnes, though these figures were later revised.
facts.quote: Originally thought to be the largest known titanosaur and land animal overall, preliminary studies and press releases suggested that Patagotitan had an estimated length of 37 m and an estimated weight of 69 tonne.

facts.statement: Later research revised the size estimates to approximately 31 meters in length and 50 to 60 tonnes in weight, making it similar to or smaller than relatives like Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus.
facts.quote: Later research revised the length estimate down to 31 m and weight estimates down to approximately 50 - 60 tonne, suggesting that Patagotitan was of a similar size to, if not smaller than, its closest relatives Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Patagotitan belongs to the clade Lognkosauria and is characterized as a large and robust titanosaur.
facts.quote: Like Argentinosaurus and other members of its clade, Lognkosauria, Patagotitan was a particularly large and robust titanosaur.

facts.statement: Patagotitan was used by Carballido and colleagues in 2022 to help redefine the group Colossosauria.
facts.quote: This led to its use in a re-definition of the group Colossosauria by Carballido and colleagues in 2022.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding Patagotitan's maximum size, with initial estimates of 37 meters and 69 tonnes later revised down to 31 meters and 50-60 tonnes, placing it potentially smaller than Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus.
facts.quote: Originally thought to be the largest known titanosaur and land animal overall, preliminary studies and press releases suggested that Patagotitan had an estimated length of 37 m and an estimated weight of 69 tonne. Later research revised the length estimate down to 31 m and weight estimates down to approximately 50 - 60 tonne, suggesting that Patagotitan was of a similar size to, if not smaller than, its closest relatives Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Patagotitan was a quadrupedal herbivore characterized by a long neck and tail.
facts.quote: Like other titanosaur sauropods, Patagotitan was a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck and tail and is notable for its large size.

facts.statement: A 2014 news report estimated Patagotitan to be 40 meters long and weigh 77 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2014 news reports provided estimates of Patagotitan size at 40 m long with a weight of 77 tonne.

facts.statement: In 2017, Carballido and colleagues estimated Patagotitan's length at 37 meters and its weight between 44.2 and 77.6 tonnes using volumetric methods.
facts.quote: In 2017, Carballido and colleagues published a length estimate of 37 m, and provided two weight estimates: 69 tonne using a scaling equation, and 44.2 - 77.6 t using volumetric method based on 3D skeletal models.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Patagotitan's length at 31 meters and weight between 50 and 55 tonnes in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019 Gregory S. Paul estimated Patagotitan at 31 m in length and 50 - 55 t in weight using volumetric models.

facts.statement: Campione and Evans estimated Patagotitan's body mass at approximately 55.7 tonnes in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, Campione and Evans yielded a body mass estimate of approximately 55.7 t.

facts.statement: Otero and Carballido estimated Patagotitan's mean weight at 57 tonnes with a margin of error between 42.5 and 71.4 tonnes in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, Otero and Carballido published a lower mean weight estimate of 57 t using a revised scaling equation, with a margin of error of 42.5 – 71.4 t

facts.statement: Histological analysis of five femora and one humerus indicates Patagotitan individuals died as young adults when growth had slowed but not stopped.
facts.quote: Histology of five femora and one humerus indicates that the individuals died while they were young adults, with growth having slowed but not ceased entirely.

facts.statement: In 2024, Paul estimated Patagotitan's length at 31 meters and weight at 57 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2024, Paul estimated its length at 31 m, and its weight at 57 t.

facts.statement: Science writer Riley Black and paleontologist Matt Wedel cautioned against the size estimates reported for Patagotitan following its 2017 publication.
facts.quote: Following the initial publication of Patagotitan in 2017, science writer Riley Black and paleontologist Matt Wedel cautioned against the reported estimates.

facts.statement: Matt Wedel criticized the polygon-based method used to compare Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus vertebrae, noting the former was largely empty space.
facts.quote: Wedel also criticised the polygon-based method that Carballido and colleagues used to compare the sizes of Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus vertebrae, noting that the former was largely empty space.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul argued in 2019 that Patagotitan could not have had a larger torso than Argentinosaurus because its articulated back vertebrae were shorter.
facts.quote: In 2019, Paul noted that the articulated length of the back vertebrae was larger in Argentinosaurus (4.47 m) than in Patagotitan (3.67 m), making it impossible for Patagotitan to have had a larger torso.

facts.statement: Matthew Dempsey estimated Patagotitan's weight at over 60 tonnes in 2025.
facts.quote: In 2025, Matthew Dempsey estimated Patagotitan weight at over 60 t.

facts.statement: Front and middle neck vertebrae of Patagotitan were at least five times longer than wide, had horizontally flattened neural spines, and lacked large pleurocoels.
facts.quote: The vertebrae in the front and middle portions of the neck of Patagotitan were very long, being at least five times as long as they were wide at the back, with neural spines on top that were horizontally flattened, and only small holes and no large pleurocoels (neurovascular openings) on the sides.

facts.statement: Patagotitan probably had 10 back vertebrae, similar to Futalognkosaurus and other titanosaurs with complete sets.
facts.quote: Like Futalognkosaurus and other titanosaurs that preserved a complete set of back vertebrae, Patagotitan probably had 10.

facts.statement: Patagotitan uniquely possessed nearly vertical prezygodiapophyseal laminae because its prezygapophyses were situated higher than its diapophyses.
facts.quote: Uniquely, the prezygodiapophyseal laminae (PRDLs, which ran between articular processes, from the prezygapophyses at the front to the diapophyses at the sides) were nearly vertical because the prezygapophyses were situated higher up on the vertebrae than the diapophyses.

facts.statement: All neural spines in Patagotitan's back were tall and vertical, with the first few having expanded, arrow-shaped ends.
facts.quote: All of the neural spines in the back were tall and vertical in Patagotitan, and the first few had expanded, arrow-shaped ends.

facts.statement: Patagotitan represents a reversal to the non-titanosauriform condition regarding the inclination of rear neural spines.
facts.quote: Patagotitan represents a reversal to the condition in non-titanosauriforms.

facts.statement: In the first two back vertebrae, Patagotitan uniquely had prespinal laminae that bulged outwards near the bottom.
facts.quote: Uniquely, in the first two back vertebrae, the prespinal laminae that ran alongside the front of the neural spines bulged outwards near the bottom.

facts.statement: The third back vertebra of Patagotitan uniquely preserves a hyposphene but not a hypantrum, suggesting the missing fourth vertebra had a corresponding hypantrum.
facts.quote: Also uniquely, the third back vertebra preserves a hyposphene at the rear end but not a hypantrum at the front; the missing fourth back vertebra presumably had a corresponding hypantrum.

facts.statement: Patagotitan uniquely had a flat front articulating surface on the first tail vertebra.
facts.quote: Uniquely in Patagotitan, the front articulating surface of the first tail vertebra was flat.

facts.statement: Patagotitan's front tail neural spines were uniquely four to six times wider than long, contrasting with other titanosaurs where they were longer front to back.
facts.quote: Also uniquely, the neural spines of the front tail vertebrae were about four to six times as wide from side to side as they were long front to back, contrasting with the condition in Dreadnoughtus, Epachthosaurus, and Malawisaurus where they were longer front to back.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Patagotitan's front tail vertebrae were 1.5 times taller than the underlying centra.
facts.quote: They were also tall, being 1.5 times taller than the underlying centra (vertebral bodies).

facts.statement: The tops of Patagotitan's front tail neural spines were uniquely concave, making them bifurcated with tips curling forwards.
facts.quote: Yet another unique characteristic was that the tops of the neural spines were concave, making them somewhat bifurcated with the tips curling forwards.

facts.statement: The transverse processes on Patagotitan's front tail vertebrae were high and thin, similar to Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus but unlike Dreadnoughtus.
facts.quote: At the sides of the front tail vertebrae, the transverse processes (on which the diapophyses were located) were high and thin, like Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus but unlike Dreadnoughtus and other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Patagotitan's expanded transverse processes provided greater muscle attachment areas, resulting in a more muscular tail.
facts.quote: These expanded transverse processes would have resulted in greater attachment areas for the caudofemoralis longus, ilio-ischiocaudalis, and spinalis muscles, and therefore a more muscular tail.

facts.statement: Patagotitan had a scapula blade that was 4.15 times as long as it was wide at its narrowest point.
facts.quote: Patagotitan had a robust, expanded scapula, with the blade being only 4.15 times as long as it was wide at its narrowest point

facts.statement: The acromion ridge on the Patagotitan scapula was about 30% as long as the scapula itself.
facts.quote: However, like other titanosaurs, the acromion ridge was about 30% as long as the scapula

facts.statement: A second projection at the beginning of the scapula blade is unique to Patagotitan among titanosaurs except for Alamosaurus, Dreadnoughtus, Drusilasaura, Elaltitan, and Sauroposeidon.
facts.quote: there was a second one further back at the beginning of the blade, only seen otherwise in Alamosaurus, Dreadnoughtus, Drusilasaura, Elaltitan, and Sauroposeidon

facts.statement: A second ridge running diagonally up the scapula blade is unique to Patagotitan.
facts.quote: there was a second ridge that ran upwards diagonally to the top of the bone, which was unique to Patagotitan

facts.statement: The articulating surface of the Patagotitan coracoid with the scapula was 80% as long front-to-back as it was tall.
facts.quote: The articulating surface of the coracoid with the scapula was 80% as long front-to-back as it was tall

facts.statement: The Patagotitan humerus was on average 28% as broad as it was long.
facts.quote: The humerus of Patagotitan was on average 28% as broad as it was long

facts.statement: A number of muscle attachment bulges on the Patagotitan humerus are unique characteristics of the species.
facts.quote: A number of bulges for muscle attachment on the humerus were unique characteristics of Patagotitan

facts.statement: The Patagotitan humerus has a pair of scars in a front upper depression where the top scar is wider than tall and the bottom scar is taller than wide.
facts.quote: In a depression (fossa) on the front upper portion of the humerus, there was a pair of scars above each other, with the top one being wider than tall and the bottom one being taller than wide

facts.statement: Behind the deltopectoral crest on the Patagotitan humerus, there is one muscle scar at the midpoint of the crest and one at the bottom.
facts.quote: On the other side of the bone, behind the deltopectoral crest on the outer side, there was one scar at the midpoint of the crest and one at the bottom

facts.statement: The Patagotitan ulna was about 50% as broad at the top as it was long.
facts.quote: The ulna was robust, being about 50% as broad at the top as it was long

facts.statement: The inward-pointing anteromedial process of the Patagotitan ulna was 3.5 times as long as it was wide and angled at 40°.
facts.quote: the inward-pointing anteromedial process of the ulna was relatively slender, being 3.5 times as long as it was wide, and was also relatively horizontal with an angle of 40°

facts.statement: The Patagotitan radius was 36% as broad at the top as it was long.
facts.quote: The radius was also fairly expanded, being 36% as broad at the top as it was long

facts.statement: A bulging scar for the biceps brachii muscle attachment on the inner edge of the Patagotitan radius extends forward as a crest.
facts.quote: On the inner edge of the radius, a bulging scar for the attachment of the biceps brachii muscle extended towards the front of the bone as a crest

facts.statement: The contact between the pubis and ischium in the Patagotitan hip girdle was about half the length of the pubis.
facts.quote: The contact between the forward-pointing pubis and backward-pointing ischium was about half of the former's length

facts.statement: The Patagotitan femur was on average 23% as broad as it was long.
facts.quote: Like the humerus, the femur of Patagotitan was robust, being on average 23% as broad as it was long

facts.statement: Uniquely among sauropods, the Patagotitan femur has a series of coarse ridges on the outer edge above the lateral condyle.
facts.quote: Uniquely among sauropods, at the outer edge of the bottom of the femur, there were a series of coarse ridges right above the articulation known as the lateral condyle

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis placed Patagotitan as the sister group to Argentinosaurus.
